skill: Identify populations, samples, parameters of interest, and statistics.
Classify a piece of data as categorical or quantitative.
Calculate and understand percentages, including pie charts.
Identify good sampling methods that use randomization.
Know the difference between observational studies and experiments, and what they can tell us.
Create and read frequency distribution tables, relative frequency distribution tables, and cumulative frequency distribution tables.
Use binning when creating frequency distribution tables.
Create (by hand and using technology) and interpret histograms of quantitative data.
Create (by hand and using technology) and interpret dotplots and stem-and-leaf plots.
Describe the shape, center, and spread of a distribution of quantitative data.
Interpret the shape of a histogram and describe the behavior of a distribution in context.
Calculate and interpret the percentile of a value.
Find the value at a given percentile.
Calculate the 5-number summary (Min, Q1, Med, Q3, Max) of a dataset.
Create and interpret boxplots.
Identify outliers using the 1.5×IQR rule.
Calculate the following measures of center and location: mean, median, mode.
Calculate and interpret the standard deviation for a set of data.
Calculate and interpret z-scores.
Use z-scores to find unusual values or compare values.
Identify the best measures of center and spread based on shape.
Compare the mean and median given the shape of a distribution.
Use basic notation and terminology for probability.
Use the general multiplication rule for AND type of probabilities.
Use the general addition rule for OR type of probabilities.
Use tree diagrams, Venn diagrams, and contingency tables to calculate probabilities.
Determine whether or not a given probability distribution is valid.
Calculate and interpret the expected value and standard deviation of a discrete probability distribution.
Determine and verify that a scenario follows a binomial distribution.
Use StatCrunch, Art of Stat, or a calculator to calculate probabilities involving a binomial distribution.
Use formulas to calculate the mean (expected value) and standard deviation of a binomial random variable.
Interpret the area under a continuous distribution (probability density function) as the probability.
Calculate probabilities of a continuous uniform distribution by finding the area of a rectangle.
Calculate probabilities of a normal distribution using the empirical rule or a normal distribution calculator (like on StatCrunch or Art of Stat).
Solve problems involving the normal distribution.
Learn to use and interpret z-scores to standardize data.
Understand what a sampling distribution is.
Know the requirements of the central limit theorem.
Know the consequences of the central limit theorem.
Use the sampling distribution of means and proportions to calculate probabilities of sample means and sample proportions.
